case: A failed InnoDB DML batch rolls back transactional rows but preserves AFTER INSERT trigger writes to MyISAM, MEMORY and CSV tables
contract: The fixture inserts ID 1 successfully, then submits a batch that inserts ID 2 and fails on duplicate ID 1.
The InnoDB parent table contains only ID 1 after the transaction rollback.
The AFTER INSERT trigger effects for IDs 1 and 2 remain visible in MyISAM, MEMORY and CSV tables.
This proves only the named MySQL engines and trigger pattern; it does not establish atomicity for all engines or side effects.

focused_test.command: rtk proxy cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-mysql --test integration mysql_atomic::mysql_batch_rollback_does_not_claim_to_reverse_nontransactional_engine_effects -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

remaining: Other non-transactional engines and trigger or side-effect patterns remain untested.
